ctx.x: But perhaps this being, as far as I know, the only really large scale study of at least a single jazz figure's technique of improvisation, suggests something about the mechanics of what improvising is.

Well, I think Parker would certainly, undoubtedly be the outstanding example, but I think this applies to almost any improvisation that I think you would hear coming out of a musician's instrument, and you would find this pattern

items.q: you did work with him on occasion in recording situations, and I believe you said you did have an opportunity to talk to him and have a conversation with him.

ctx.x: For me, yes. For me, yes, Coltrane notwithstanding. I’m sure he made a valuable contribution, but, you know, I think Parker did it. I’m still amazed by it.

While we’re on the subject of Charlie Parker, you did work with him on occasion in recording situations, and I believe you said you did have an opportunity to talk to him and have a conversation with him.
Rather brief, but nonetheless we did, yeah.
